task: Finalize this PrismShelf manifest reference for museum metadata integrators who often arrive through bookmarked field headings. Keep the page limited to the package manifest format and its validation. Preserve the published object-key, view, and asset-path fragment destinations and the supplemental reference links.
source_facts: PrismShelf 3.2 is a synthetic museum image-package validator. The following specification is authoritative and supplies all technical facts needed for this page. The audience prepares packages for a museum catalog; this page is a lookup reference, not a catalog installation guide. Readers enter directly at bookmarked field sections. Existing fragment destinations object-key, view, and asset-path must continue to work. A package directory contains a UTF-8 CSV manifest named views.csv. Its required header is exactly object_key,view,asset_path in that order. Each data row relates one catalog object, one photographic perspective, and one image file. The object_key field is the catalog accession identifier, not the image filename. Object keys are case-sensitive: A104 and a104 are different identifiers. The view field identifies the photographic perspective and permits exactly front, back, or detail, in lowercase. View labels do not describe public visibility. The pair (object_key, view) must be unique within the manifest. Therefore A104/front and A104/back may coexist; a second A104/front is invalid even if it names a different image. A duplicate pair is reported as duplicate_view. Pair uniqueness is a manifest-level rule, not a prohibition on showing multiple perspectives of one accession. The asset_path field names an image file relative to the package directory, not relative to the shell's current directory or a public website. Absolute paths are invalid. Parent-directory traversal segments (..) are invalid. A blank asset_path is invalid rather than an instruction to reuse an earlier row. The validator requires the named image file to be present in the package. Paths are literal local package references, not download URLs. For the example package exhibit-demo, the front image is exhibit-demo/images/A104-front.tif; its row uses images/A104-front.tif. The illustrative rows are A104,front,images/A104-front.tif and A104,back,images/A104-back.tif. They are valid together when the package contains those files and the catalog contains A104. The row A104,front,images/A104-front-crop.tif would duplicate the first row's identity even though the image path differs. Before validation, the package must be associated with a sealed catalog snapshot through the museum's existing catalog preparation process. A sealed snapshot fixes the set of accession identifiers against which the manifest is checked. An unsealed snapshot blocks validation. Sealing a snapshot does not certify image quality. There is no snapshot creation command on this reference page. Run `pshelf validate --package exhibit-demo` after package readiness is satisfied. Validation is read-only: it reports results without changing the package. It is not a catalog publication action. The diagnostic missing_asset means a referenced image file is absent from the package. unknown_object means the accession is absent from the associated sealed snapshot. These are different from duplicate_view. The name views.csv and the header are format requirements; the example directory exhibit-demo and accession A104 are illustrative. Field descriptions, examples, and error explanations can be presented in any equivalent structure without requiring a single reading order. `catalog-snapshots.md` documents the existing snapshot preparation process and `package-layout.md` documents package directory layout. These are useful supplemental references; the readiness condition, field definitions, path rules, examples, and diagnostic meanings needed here must be available on this page.
draft: # PrismShelf 3.2 image manifest reference ## Worked rows A package can contain `A104,front,images/A104-front.tif` and `A104,back,images/A104-back.tif` together. These rows let a museum record more than one photographic perspective of the same object. They assume that the package contains both image files and that the associated catalog snapshot contains A104. The directory used in this page is exhibit-demo; substitute your package directory when validating your own material. The accession A104 is also illustrative rather than an identifier that every museum must create. Run `pshelf validate --package exhibit-demo` to check a prepared package. The validator reports results without changing the package. This is a read-only check, not an operation that publishes images to the museum catalog. A successful check therefore does not mean that a public catalog page has been created. ## Collision diagnostics `duplicate_view` reports a repeated object-and-view pair. A row naming `images/A104-front-crop.tif` still collides with the first worked row if it uses A104 and front. Changing only the image filename does not give that row a new identity. This diagnostic concerns how a row is identified in the manifest, so replacing an image path without changing the pair does not address the reason for the rejection. ## Asset location The field `asset_path` names an image file relative to the package directory. It is not relative to the directory from which an integrator happens to invoke the validator. For exhibit-demo, the row value `images/A104-front.tif` points to `exhibit-demo/images/A104-front.tif`. This relationship allows the manifest and its image directory to be handled as one package. See [Package layout](package-layout.md) for the directory-layout reference used alongside this page. ## Header and encoding Name the manifest `views.csv` and encode it as UTF-8 CSV. The required header is `object_key,view,asset_path`, in that order. The header identifies the three positions used by each data row; a reader should not infer the column order from the visual shape of a filename. The name views.csv is a format requirement, unlike the example package name exhibit-demo. Keeping those two kinds of names distinct matters when adapting a worked example for a new exhibition package. ## Object identity `object_key` is the museum catalog accession identifier. It selects the catalog object represented by the row rather than naming the image file. One accession can therefore appear in several rows describing different photographic perspectives. An integrator looking up this field may need the catalog's accession value even when the photographer has used a descriptive filename. The file and catalog identifiers serve different roles in the same record and are not interchangeable simply because an example uses similar text in both. ## Package readiness Before validation, the package must be associated with a sealed catalog snapshot through the museum's existing preparation process. An unsealed snapshot blocks validation. The sealed snapshot fixes the set of accession identifiers against which the manifest is checked; sealing does not certify the quality of the photographs. Use [Catalog snapshots](catalog-snapshots.md) for the preparation process. This reference supplies the required readiness condition but does not introduce a snapshot creation command or replace the museum's catalog preparation instructions. ## What the file describes Each row relates one catalog object, one photographic perspective, and one image file. The manifest is part of a package directory. It gives the validator those relationships in a form it can check against the associated catalog snapshot and the files in the package. Integrators use this page to look up a particular field, interpret a rejected row, or adapt an example. The field destinations remain useful when a support ticket links directly to a specific definition. ## Path restrictions An absolute path is invalid in the image-file field. A path containing a parent-directory traversal segment, `..`, is also invalid. The named image must be present in the package; the value is a literal local reference, not a download URL. A blank value is invalid and does not ask the validator to reuse the image from the previous row. When diagnosing a path, distinguish the recorded relative value from the complete filesystem location obtained by placing it under the package directory. ## View vocabulary The `view` field identifies photographic perspective. Its permitted values are exactly `front`, `back`, and `detail`, written in lowercase. These labels do not describe whether an image is publicly visible. A detail image still belongs to the same catalog object identified by its row's accession. The perspective label allows the catalog relationship to distinguish it from that object's front or back image without making a new accession for each photograph. ## Identifier comparison Object keys are case-sensitive: A104 and a104 are different identifiers. The pair `(object_key, view)` must be unique within one manifest. Multiple perspectives of one accession are allowed, but a second row using the same accession and perspective is not. Pair uniqueness is a manifest-level condition, rather than a restriction requiring one photograph per museum object. ## Missing references `missing_asset` means the referenced image file is absent from the package. `unknown_object` means the accession is absent from the associated sealed snapshot. Those diagnostics point to different relationships: one connects the manifest to a local image, and the other connects it to the catalog. Neither diagnostic is another name for `duplicate_view`. Use the reported condition to decide which relationship to investigate instead of assuming that every rejected row has an incorrect filename. For example, a sealed snapshot containing A104 but not a104 cannot resolve a row whose object key is a104, even if that row points to an existing image. The image's presence does not supply the missing catalog identity. Conversely, an accession found in the snapshot does not supply an image that is missing from the package. These distinctions help an integrator direct a question to the catalog preparation work or to the image package without confusing the two kinds of evidence.

requirements.description: The required CSV header order is object_key,view,asset_path.
The catalog-identifier field is named object_key.
The catalog-identifier field means the object's accession identifier rather than its image filename.
The view field means photographic perspective rather than public visibility.
The permitted view values are exactly front, back, and detail in lowercase.
The object_key and view pair must be unique within a manifest.
The asset_path value is relative to the package directory.
Parent-directory traversal segments are invalid in asset_path.
Association with a sealed catalog snapshot is required before validation.
Preserve the validation invocation pshelf validate --package exhibit-demo.
Validation does not modify the package.
The diagnostic duplicate_view denotes a repeated object-and-view pair.
The front and back rows for A104 may coexist in the same manifest.
The published asset-path fragment destination must remain valid.

issues.description: The object identity, case comparison, and pair-uniqueness rules are dispersed among Object identity, Identifier comparison, and Collision diagnostics without field-level navigation joining them.
issues.acceptable_resolution: Make the related identity rules accessible from the bookmarked field sections through grouping or targeted cross-references. Do not require readers to start at the top or remove useful field destinations.

issues.acceptable_resolution: Provide an intelligible lookup structure with a discoverable format overview and access to all path rules from the path entry point. A table, grouped sections, or another reference structure is acceptable; a linear tutorial is not required.
